sourceOccurrences.label: Finite-modification invariance on an arbitrary coordinate set
sourceOccurrences.note: D1CH retains measurability and pointwise insertion equivalence, derives deletion and finite-modification invariance, and proves the outside-finite-set tail property and zero-one conclusion. It generalizes the product-space step of H0OC without removing the graph event measurability requirement. No countability of the coordinate set or strict interior profile assumption is added.

sourceOccurrences.label: Finite-cylinder approximation, mixing and invariant observables
sourceOccurrences.note: DK14 preserves arbitrary finite measures for approximation. MJD2 preserves law invariance and eventual finite-set separation, and proves the collision criterion and profile-invariance sufficient conditions. DRQ2 gives event ergodicity and constancy of measurable extended-integer observables; no boundedness or integrability is assumed. The lattice application specializes to non-loop coordinates and links the existing 6GNC argument; no new uniqueness result or compiled association is claimed.

sourceOccurrences.label: Translation ergodicity of bond laws on infinite groups
sourceOccurrences.note: WUAF retains arbitrary infinite groups, right translations and profile invariance including diagonal pairs, with explicit measurability of events/observables. Distinct translations give at most two collisions per fixed pair. Mixing along such a sequence and the diagonal-erasure graph extension are expository consequences. The integer nonempty-configuration witness concerns raw pair coordinates, not percolation. No compiled correspondence is asserted.

sourceOccurrences.label: Global percolation and finite modifications
sourceOccurrences.note: D106 and H0OC provide the deterministic finite-change proof and the countable global zero-one law. The source permits the empty vertex type as well; its event is empty and has probability zero. It does not give a rooted zero-one law, uniqueness or spatial ergodicity.

sourceOccurrences.label: A global threshold attained by no root
sourceOccurrences.note: Thirteen public results construct the bounded-degree disjoint-tree example and identify its rooted and global parameter sets. Source pin: 3978a2fa0ec425729f6e15fbc3c6a142cfa4a672.

proofUses.reason: Deleting or adding one edge changes components finitely; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
A positive root probability makes the global probability positive and hence one by the global zero-one law (H0OC); the converse is countable subadditivity.
The global event is a countable union of root events; the positive-path comparison (C3OO) makes rooted thresholds equal within each support component.
Finite-modification invariance places A in every outside sigma-algebra, and approximation by a finite-coordinate event (DK14) gives P(A)=P(A)^2.
